ca_east_face_3.blurb: The east-facing side of Dike Wall sits above Lake George in the Mammoth Lakes area, at roughly 9,350 feet. It is a tall, slightly steep wall with nine routes: six bolted lines and three alpine-style routes, including a trad dihedral. Difficulty runs from about 5.10 into the low 5.12s, with most of the sport climbing in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on steeper rock. The face picks up sun early in the day. The walk up from the lake ends with a short talus field below the first routes.

ca_batman_boulder.blurb: Batman Boulder is the first climbable block you meet along Trabuco Creek Road in the Santa Ana Mountains of Orange County. It has nine problems, running from easy V0 to a hard V7 line, with the bulk of them between V1 and V5. A large overhang and a stand of tall bamboo throw some shade between attempts. Several of the problems are sit starts and stand-start variations. It is a compact, single-boulder stop that combines well with the other blocks scattered through the creek bed further along the road.

ca_dark_colored_cliffs_2.blurb: Dark-Colored Cliffs is a small dry-tooling and mixed venue at the upper end of the Narrows in Lee Vining Canyon, on the Eastern Sierra side of Yosemite. A talus fan at creek level separates it from the pale cliffs beside it. Eight of its nine climbs are mixed, spanning easy M3 up to M9-, with a single WI3 ice line among them. Routes combine bolts and gear placements, so a rack and screws can both be useful. It is the harder, more technical end of the canyon, with room left for new lines.

ca_jellystone_northeast_face.blurb: The northeast face of Jellystone is the steeper of the two main faces at this Joshua Tree formation in the Lost Horse area, a short way west of Quail Springs Road. It looks toward the road and is the first wall you see on the usual walk in, roughly 100 to 200 yards from Pet Rock. Nine routes are here: eight trad lines and one top-rope, with grades from 5.7 up to 5.11. Most are in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, which makes it a reasonable stop for moderate trad leaders.

ca_bald_eagle_peak.blurb: Bald Eagle Peak is a small crag southwest of Lake Isabella on the northern edge of the Piute Mountains in the southern Sierra, at around 6,000 feet in Sequoia National Forest. It offers nine routes, five trad and four sport, mostly graded 5.10 with a couple of 5.9s and a lone 5.11. Single-pitch and multi-pitch lines are both on offer, and most bolted routes have chained anchors. The walls see few visitors.

ca_7_up_and_down_wall.blurb: Up And Down Wall is the last of the numbered walls in the Marble Caves, a limestone area in northwest California above the South Fork of the Trinity River. It is the farthest on the trail from the road, a bit over 20 minutes on foot, with a few large trees giving some shade at the base. All nine routes are bolted, running from 5.10a to 5.12b with the weight in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Expect a committed walk, but you get a full set of mid-grade sport pitches at the end of it.
